references.text: The context for Jesus' words to Martha: she had welcomed Jesus into her home and was busy with all the preparations, while her sister Mary sat at Jesus' feet to listen.
Jesus speaks about not worrying (μεριμνάω) about food, drink, and clothing. The same Greek word for worry is used here as in Luke 10:41, where Martha is worried about many things.
Paul urges: "Be anxious for nothing" (μηδὲν μεριμνᾶτε) – the same theme of anxiety that Jesus addresses toward Martha.
"Cast all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you." The point is the same as in Jesus' words to Martha: entrusting our worries to God.
In the parable of the sower, worry (μέριμνα) about this world chokes the Word. Jesus warns against the same kind of worry that Martha displays.
Jesus warns his disciples that their hearts must not be weighed down by life's anxieties (μέριμναι). The same theme as the warning to Martha.
Jesus tells his disciples not to worry (μεριμνᾶτε) about life, what they should eat or wear – a parallel to the warning given to Martha about her many worries.

In Luke's version of the parable of the sower, the Word is choked by anxieties (μεριμνῶν) and wealth. Worry hinders spiritual growth, just as Martha's busy preparations kept her from listening to Jesus.

The Preacher speaks that what the eyes see is better than the restless wandering of the soul – a wisdom saying reflecting the theme of worrying about many things versus focusing on the one thing needed.
Paul writes about being free from anxiety (ἀμέριμνος) and undivided in devotion to the Lord, without distraction – the same point Jesus makes toward Martha.
